study: Book walls / room to run: at a random entry minute, does an OPEN ask side (no large resting ask within +15 bp of the mid) predict a larger 5-minute rise than a WALLED one (a large ask within +15 bp), and does bid SUPPORT (a large resting bid within -15 bp) predict a larger rise than none - by >= +5 bp?
registered_at: 2026-10-22, before any wall feature is computed
origin: Operator 10/22: when the desk had Webull Level 2 (July 2026, OpenAPI depth=10 plus OCR of the app book) they read big asks as ceilings that block profit runs and stacked bids as support, i.e. room to run. The 10/4 depth test reduced the book to one imbalance number (OBI5 = top-5 bid vs ask size); where size sits (walls, open sky, support) was never tested. The exit study says the desk's money is in fast runs (capture 0.71-0.78 of a 3-minute run; break-even entry edge ~+11 bp).
prior: LOW (~8-12%). Displayed walls are often pulled (spoofing), Nasdaq's book is one venue (~15-20% of volume), the 10/4 imbalance gate was slightly negative (-3.3 / -0.6 bp at 120 s), and ASK_THIN30 (asks draining) read +1.8 / -0.1 bp as information. In favour: 'resistance from resting size' is a distinct feature from total imbalance, and the market-microstructure literature finds that large visible depth slows price movement through it.

data.source: Already on the mini, bought 10/4 (no new spend): data/databento/xnas_itch_mbp10_2026-06_08/. Databento XNAS.ITCH mbp-10 (Nasdaq's own book, top 10 levels each side, every row carries the full snapshot) for [signal - 35 s, signal] by ts_recv, 7,353 random entries (seed 17, 3 per name-day, 09:45-15:29 ET) on the day's 40 largest gappers (open >= $10 by the daily file, prior-day dollar volume >= $20M, gap >= +2%), 63 sessions 2026-06-01 .. 08-28. Outcomes: Alpaca SIP NBBO cached in sip_quotes.json at signal + 0.5 s and + 0.5 s + 60 / 120 / 300 s (0 lookup failures).
data.already_seen: This dataset's OUTCOMES were read on 10/4 for the imbalance features (OBI5, OBI1, ASK_THIN30, by hour, 60/120/300 s). No wall, room or support feature has been computed. Because the sample is not fresh, a PASS here is a LEAD only and needs forward confirmation (below) before any desk use.
data.book_rules: As the 10/4 study (features.json drops): the book at time S is the last mbp-10 row with ts_recv <= S; no_book / stale (> 30 s old) / halt rows are dropped (7,261 survivors). Prices NaN = level absent.

population: Entries with SIP mid at signal + 0.5 s >= $20 (the desk's live floor since 10/21; also removes the 140 entries under $10 that the daily file's bad prices let in) and a valid book. Not spread-capped (the median quoted spread on this sample is 14 bp; the spread-capped subset is information).

features.wall: At the snapshot at the signal: an ask (bid) level whose displayed size >= 4 x the median displayed size of all present levels on both sides of that snapshot (up to 20 levels). Within-snapshot, so no look-ahead and no name-size scaling.
features.visible_range: ask side: (10th present ask level price / mid - 1); bid side: (1 - 10th present bid level price / mid). An entry is CLASSIFIABLE on a side if a wall is seen within 15 bp of the mid on that side OR the visible range on that side reaches >= 15 bp (so the absence of a wall is observed, not assumed). Unclassifiable entries are counted per price stratum and excluded from that hypothesis (declared: this drops many high-priced thick-book names whose 10 levels span < 15 bp).
features.H1_groups: OPEN = ask-classifiable and no ask wall with price <= mid x (1 + 15 bp); WALLED = an ask wall within +15 bp.
features.H2_groups: SUPPORTED = bid-classifiable and a bid wall with price >= mid x (1 - 15 bp); UNSUPPORTED = bid-classifiable and none.

outcome: PRIMARY: gross mid-to-mid return from signal + 0.5 s to signal + 0.5 s + 300 s (SIP NBBO mids). Why 300 s: the desk holds 3-8 minutes and the question is room for a run; 60 / 120 s are information. NET (buy at the ask, sell at the bid) is reported; the absolute check uses the desk's cost (gross - 5 bp), because this gapper sample's quoted spreads (median 14 bp) are not the desk's spread-capped names.
statistic: Per hypothesis and half: per day, mean gross of the favoured group (OPEN; SUPPORTED) minus mean gross of the other group (days with >= 3 entries in each group); day-equal mean, day-clustered t (df = days - 1).
multiplicity: 2 tests (H1, H2): one-sided t_crit at 0.025 / 2, df = days - 1.
power: Outcome-blind count step before any outcome is read: per hypothesis and half, group sizes, days with >= 3 in each group, unclassifiable shares by price stratum, and a projected MDE from the 300 s gross of SEEDED RANDOM group labels of the same sizes (a label permutation, which reads outcomes but no feature-outcome link). Floors per half: >= 300 entries in each group and >= 20 days; otherwise UNDERPOWERED.
pass: Per hypothesis, in BOTH halves: lift >= +5 bp with t >= t_crit; favoured-group mean gross - 5 bp > 0 (day-equal); WITHIN-NAME-DAY lift >= 0 (name-days with entries in both groups: mean of favoured minus other within the name-day, then day-equal) - this guards against the groups being different kinds of names; dropping the 3 days and (separately) the 3 names with the largest share keeps lift >= 0. FAIL: t <= -2 in a half, or the 97.5% upper bound < +5 bp in both halves (whenever each half has >= 2 days). Otherwise UNDERPOWERED. PASS = LEAD (not fresh data).
placebo: Before scoring: the same statistic with group labels shuffled within each day (seeded), |t| within the two-sided t_crit in both halves, for H1 and H2; else --score refuses.
information_only: PULLED vs HELD walls: an ask wall within +15 bp at signal - 30 s that is gone (< half its size, or price level absent) at the signal vs one still there; and walls that appear in the last 30 s
room as a continuous number (bp to the first ask wall, censored at the visible range) - lift by tercile
OPEN and SUPPORTED together vs WALLED and UNSUPPORTED
60 s and 120 s horizons; net after the quoted spread
spread-capped subset (quoted spread <= 10 bp) and price strata ($20-50, $50+)
added value over OBI5_dm (the lift within OBI5_dm terciles)
wall multiplier 3x and 6x, and a +10 / +25 bp window
confirmation: A PASS is a LEAD. It is confirmed only forward on the desk's own board names with a recorded live depth feed (e.g. Webull OpenAPI Advanced Quotes depth=10, about $3/month, an operator decision under 'no spend until proven'), >= 20 sessions, same code, before any desk use.
no_retuning: 4x wall multiplier, 15 bp window, 300 s, the $20 floor, the halves, the floors and the >= 3-per-group day rule are fixed.
declared_deviations: random minutes on gappers, not the desk's entries
Nasdaq's book only (one venue); the desk's Webull L2 showed the same Nasdaq data
only 10 levels each side: walls further away are invisible; handled by the classifiable rule
the entry is at the mid in the gross outcome; the desk pays its own spread
script: tools/studies/book_walls.py (to be written): features from the mbp-10 files (dbn venv), count step, placebo, --score after a result-skeptic READY.
amended: 2026-10-22, before any script or wall feature, after result-skeptic FIX FIRST (9 items). (1) WINDOW FROM THE TOUCH: the ask window is [best ask, best ask x (1 + 15 bp)], the bid window [best bid x (1 - 15 bp), best bid]; POPULATION adds a spread cap: Nasdaq-book quoted spread at the signal <= 10 bp (the desk caps at 5 bp; 10 keeps power). (2) WALL = a level with size >= 4 x the median present-level size (both sides, that snapshot) AND notional (size x price) >= $25,000 (odd lots on high-priced names are not walls). (3) ONE CLASSIFIABLE RULE for both groups: a side is classified only if its 10th present level lies at or beyond the window edge (the whole 15 bp window is visible), whether or not a wall is seen; otherwise unclassifiable (counted by price stratum). (4) POWER BAR: the count step projects the MDE of the primary statistic; if it is > 5 bp in either half, the hypothesis stops UNDERPOWERED and is NOT scored. Stated now: with 3 entries per name-day and the spread cap this is the LIKELY outcome. (5) PRIMARY STATISTIC = the NAME-DAY FIXED-EFFECT lift: in name-days with entries in both groups (mixed), the favoured-group mean minus the other-group mean, averaged per day, day-clustered t (df = days - 1); floors per half: >= 100 mixed name-days and >= 20 days with one. The cross-sectional day-level lift (favoured - other across all entries) is information. (6) PLACEBO = permutation: labels shuffled WITHIN name-day 1,000 times (seeded 'book-walls-perm'); a PASS also needs the real lift above the permutation's 97.5th percentile in both halves (reported for all outcomes, not a gate on scoring). (7) OBI OVERLAP: a PASS also needs the fixed-effect lift >= 0 within each OBI5_dm tercile (cuts from half A) in both halves. (8) The $20 floor uses the Nasdaq-book mid at the signal, not the SIP mid at + 0.5 s. (9) FORWARD CONFIRMATION (only after a PASS): random minutes on the desk's board names (not desk fills - ~12 fills a session cannot detect 5 bp), live Nasdaq depth recorded (e.g. Webull OpenAPI depth=10), same code and bar, run until its own count step projects MDE <= 5 bp (expected 40+ sessions). Information cells (multipliers, windows, pulled walls, terciles, strata, horizons) can never be promoted to a lead. PASS conditions now: per hypothesis in BOTH halves: fixed-effect lift >= +5 bp with t >= t_crit; favoured-group mean gross - 5 bp > 0; lift above the permutation 97.5th percentile; >= 0 in each OBI5_dm tercile; drop-3 days / names >= 0. FAIL: t <= -2 in a half or 97.5% upper bound < +5 bp in both halves. Halt / stale / no-book drops follow features.json from 10/4 (halts cover the full 300.5 s).
